properties.name: Tall el-Hammam (TeH / Tell el-Hammam)
properties.location: Eastern lower Jordan Valley, NE of Dead Sea, Amman Governorate, Jordan (~12.6 km NE of Dead Sea; ~11.7 km E of Jordan River)
properties.shows: A Middle Bronze Age destruction/abandonment horizon exists at TeH with ash, collapsed architecture, and unusual heat-affected pottery/mudbrick reported by excavators. Proponents argued these matched a Tunguska-scale airburst ~1650 BCE. Scientific Reports published that claim in 2021.
properties.does_not: DOES NOT establish a confirmed cosmic airburst. Jaret & Harris (2022) argued mineralogic/geochemical data fail impact-diagnostic criteria (shocked quartz not convincingly demonstrated; high-temp melts/geochemistry not uniquely extraterrestrial). Boslough & Bruno (2025) showed Tunguska comparisons overestimated blast temperature/wind and cannot produce claimed melting at stated distances. Image-manipulation concerns were raised (Bik / Retraction Watch). Scientific Reports RETRACTED the Bunch et al. paper on 24 Apr 2025 (doi:10.1038/s41598-025-99265-5). Authors largely disagreed and later republished expanded versions elsewhere (e.g. Airbursts and Cratering Impacts / ScienceOpen). Mainstream archaeology does not accept the airburst conclusion.
properties.genesis_link: AUTHOR CLAIM (Collins/Silvia/some Bunch coauthors): TeH = Sodom; airburst mirrors 'fire from heaven' / salt narrative. Bunch et al. said Sodom ID was beyond paper's scope but speculated oral tradition. ARCHAEOLOGICAL CONSENSUS: Sodom ID not accepted; airburst paper retracted; TeH remains a major MBA Jordan Valley site with debated destruction cause.
properties.researchers: Bunch et al. 2021 Sci Rep 11:18632 doi:10.1038/s41598-021-97778-3 [RETRACTED 2025]; Author Correction 2022 doi:10.1038/s41598-022-06266-9; Retraction Note 2025 doi:10.1038/s41598-025-99265-5; Jaret & Harris 2022 Sci Rep 12:5189 doi:10.1038/s41598-022-08216-x; Boslough & Bruno 2025 Sci Rep 15:13869 doi:10.1038/s41598-025-98362-9; Silvia (Trinity Southwest / TeH team); Collins (TeH director); expanded republication ScienceOpen doi:10.14293/ACI.2025.0003; hydrocode modeling doi:10.14293/ACI.2024.0005
properties.notes: As of research date (2026-09-30): original Sci Rep airburst paper is RETRACTED. Cross-link: sodom-gomorrah-airburst-evidence.md

properties.name: Tall el-Hammam (TeH / Tell el-Hammam)
properties.location: Eastern lower Jordan Valley, NE of Dead Sea, Jordan
properties.shows: TeH sits in a seismically active rift setting where earthquakes can destroy mudbrick cities. Collapse and fire are geologically plausible. No published TeH-specific paleoseismic trench study uniquely tying the MBA horizon to a dated quake was found in this research pass.
properties.does_not: No diagnostic TeH seismite or fault rupture published that uniquely dates the MBA destruction. Earthquake is a general regional possibility, not a demonstrated TeH event. Does not prove Genesis narrative.
properties.genesis_link: Indirect only: some popular/geological writers link Dead Sea earthquakes to Genesis imagery. For TeH specifically, Collins favors catastrophic cosmic/fire scenario over ordinary quake. Consensus: seismic hazard real; biblical ID unproven.
properties.researchers: Regional paleoseismology: Ken-Tor et al. 2001 JGR doi:10.1029/2000JB900313 (Ze'elim seismites); Neev & Emery 1995 Oxford (regional fault framework). TeH airburst proponents argued against ordinary earthquake as sole cause of claimed ultra-high-temp melts.
properties.notes: Mechanism plausible regionally; site-specific published proof for MBA TeH earthquake event not established in sources reviewed.

properties.name: Bab edh-Dhra (Bab adh-Dhra')
properties.location: Southeastern Dead Sea plain (southern Ghor), Karak region, Jordan; S bank of Wadi al-Karak near Lisan peninsula
properties.shows: Major EB III occupation ended with fire damage in parts of the town and cemetery charnel houses (~c. 2350–2300 BCE per Rast/Schaub). Site suffered exposure to fire; later limited EB IV occupation outside ruined fortifications. Large EB cemetery (shaft tombs, charnel houses).
properties.does_not: Does NOT show airburst, shocked minerals, nanodiamonds, or cosmic geochemistry in published excavation literature. Fire extent debated—some summaries say Bab edh-Dhra lacked the intense site-wide conflagration seen at Numeira. Cause could be accident, attack, earthquake-triggered fire, or ritual burning of charnel houses. Human remains mainly in cemetery, not a city-wide skeletal catastrophe layer.
properties.genesis_link: AUTHOR CLAIM (Rast later nuance; Wood/ABR; van Hattem): Bab edh-Dhra often proposed as Sodom (or one of Cities of the Plain). Rast suggested tradition may stem from Bab edh-Dhra + Numeira pair. CONSENSUS: plausible southern candidate for some biblical archaeologists; not proven; chronology (EB III vs MBA patriarch dates) is a major objection for others.
properties.researchers: Rast & Schaub EDSP; Bab edh-Dhra' Excavations at the Town Site 1975–1981 (Eisenbrauns 2003); Schaub & Rast cemetery volume 1989; Rast ABD 'Bab Edh-Dhra'; Lapp 1960s cemetery digs; Chesson & Schaub 2007 Crossing Jordan chapters
properties.notes: No published airburst lab suite for this site found in this research. Classic southern Sodom candidate.

properties.name: Bab edh-Dhra (Bab adh-Dhra')

properties.genesis_link: Some authors (e.g. Klein) read Genesis as memory of rapid climatic desiccation turning a fertile plain into salt wasteland. Speculative; not site-specific proof.

properties.name: Numeira (Numayra / an-Numayra)
properties.location: Southeastern Dead Sea shore, ~13 km S of Bab edh-Dhra, Jordan; S bank of Wadi Numeira; ~280 m below sea level
properties.shows: Clear, intense fire destructions during EB III. Final burn ended occupation; site not reoccupied. ~0.5 ha walled town (~30% excavated 1977–1983). Strong archaeological evidence of catastrophic fire—stronger site-wide burn signature than often attributed to Bab edh-Dhra.
properties.does_not: No published airburst mineral suite (shocked quartz, nanodiamonds, Pt anomaly) for Numeira found. Fire cause unresolved (earthquake, attack, accident). Destruction date debated (~2600 vs ~2350/2300 BCE vs Udd's lowered dates); not simultaneous with Bab edh-Dhra if ~250 yr gap accepted. Small size challenges 'city' language.
properties.genesis_link: AUTHOR CLAIM (Wood/ABR; some EDSP-era popularizers): Numeira = Gomorrah. CONSENSUS: candidate only; chronological gap with Bab edh-Dhra and EB vs MBA debate weaken pair-as-Sodom/Gomorrah model for many scholars.
properties.researchers: Coogan BASOR reports; Rast & Schaub EDSP; Chesson, Schaub & Rast Numayra monograph (Eisenbrauns); Donahue geologic reconstruction BASOR 255 (1984); Expedition Dead Sea Plain site page
properties.notes: Best southern-Ghor example of excavated fiery destruction among Cities-of-the-Plain candidates.

properties.name: Ghor es-Safi / Zoara (biblical Zoar tradition)
properties.location: Southeastern Dead Sea, lowest part of Rift Valley, Jordan (Ghor as-Safi); traditional Zoar/Zoara
properties.shows: Long-lived oasis/settlement zone identified with biblical Zoar in Christian/classical tradition (city Lot fled to). Politis-led work documents rich multi-period archaeology. EB presence exists (cemetery etc.) but not a single famous Genesis-19 destruction excavation like Numeira.
properties.does_not: Does not provide a published airburst or unique fiery destruction proving Sodom's sister-city catastrophe. Traditional Zoar survival in Genesis complicates models that sink all cities under the lake.
properties.genesis_link: Strongest traditional link is to Zoar (escaped city), not Sodom. Used geographically to anchor southern Cities of the Plain. Consensus on Zoar tradition stronger than on Sodom ID of any one tell.
properties.researchers: Politis Ancient Landscapes of Zoara I (Routledge); ACOR Zoara chapter; Rast & Schaub survey listing Safi among five EB sites; Albright 1924 Moab/Dead Sea expedition
properties.notes: Tag = traditional/archaeological multi-period site without airburst claim. 'Destruction' not the main published story.

creation_ministry.blurb: AiG southern-Sodom article cites Zoar south of the Dead Sea (Lot’s refuge; later Madaba Map tradition) against northern TeH models. Theme/site-adjacent ministry geography—not a Zoar excavation report.
